target_customer: Non-programmers, students and educators building native mobile apps
problem: Building iOS and Android apps requires coding skill; Thunkable offers drag-and-drop no-code building.

founders.name: Arun Saigal
education: MIT, 2013 and master's 2013 per MIT News
founders.background_notes: Worked on MIT App Inventor from 2011; Forbes 30 Under 30 per YC page.

founders.name: WeiHua Li
education: MIT, 2014 and master's 2016 per MIT News
founders.background_notes: Worked on MIT App Inventor with Saigal.

competitors.name: MIT App Inventor
competitors.what: Open-source block-based app builder from which Thunkable was forked

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on App Inventor open source code, cross-platform native output is harder than web builders.

defensibility.rationale: Users store apps on platform; builder competition is wide.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it; it remains independent as of 2026.

market_need_then: MIT App Inventor had grown beyond academic resources per founders; demand for non-coder app building was visible via its user base.

branding.name_origin: The company says it comes from thunk, both a programming term and a sound, with the tagline If you can think it, you can Thunk it.

identity.logo: Official logos and badges on a press page; style guide exists

branding.brand_signature: If you can think it, you can Thunk it
branding.community_and_virality: Active forum described by MIT News; blog features creators and student competitions.

brand_strength.rationale: Playful coined name with a clear tagline and an active community, but no evidence it drove growth by itself.

pivots.why: AI trend; beta December 2025, full release February 2026 per release notes

outcome_analysis: Thunkable commercialized MIT App Inventor in YC Winter 2016, raised about 3.3 million dollars by mid 2018 and a 30 million Series B in April 2022, reporting 3 million users and 6 million apps. It remains independent and has added AI app generation. Founders with direct App Inventor experience gave domain fit; revenue and valuation are not public.
notes: A 3.3M raise from Lightspeed, NEA, SV Angel, YC and others appears in a 2018 press release but its date is not stated, so not recorded as a dated round. Total 41M per TechCrunch. A blog claim of 30M total is likely wrong. No Series A found. Founding year 2015 (YC) vs 2016 launch. Pivot date approximate. No dated competitor list beyond MIT App Inventor found. Round added: 2018-06-05 press release gives $3.3M raised to date and investors but no round stage or round amount, and CB Insights lists a Series A on 2018-06-05 with no amount, so the amount is null. Series B lead Owl Ventures per Thunkable's blog.
